trust_decision.summary: Whether an inbound webhook may trigger workflow runs is decided in two layers: autobuildService.ProcessWebhook validates the payload against the per-provider key in the openchoreo-control-plane/git-webhook-secrets Secret (HMAC/token validation is the ONLY authentication on POST /api/v1alpha1/autobuild, which is declared security: []), and webhookProcessor.findAffectedComponents decides which components that authenticated event is allowed to build.

landing_point.why: The summary 'unauthenticated build/workflow trigger via git-provider confusion (webhook signature bypass)' leads straight to the Bitbucket provider, where an empty token is explicitly accepted (`if token == "" { return nil }`) under a TODO saying HMAC validation is not implemented, and the handler never passes a signature for Bitbucket (webhook_handler.go:58-59).

fix_sites.module_kind: provider_implementation (deduplicated into shared helper; gains fail-closed empty-secret)
domain_logic (authenticated provider vs component repository host)

fix_sites.entry_point: generated client for the same route

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Bitbucket never sent a signature header, and the header-detection helper plus the OpenAPI/generated-param layer are 'just plumbing' - the reported bypass lives inside BitbucketProvider.ValidateWebhookPayload, so the composition layer can be left untouched.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Genuine Bitbucket deliveries (which do carry X-Hub-Signature) must still be accepted, and components whose repository lives on a self-hosted GitLab/GitHub Enterprise host - where the provider cannot be inferred from the host - must still have builds triggered. A fail-closed-only fix rejects every real Bitbucket webhook; an over-strict repository check stops self-hosted installs from ever building.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: internal/openchoreo-api/services/autobuild/webhook_processor.go:340-351 (self-hosted hosts deliberately supported) and fix.diff:1396-1397 (unknown host -> no provider check)

O6_input_shapes: Bitbucket signature as 'sha256=<hex>' HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body, sent in the new X-Hub-Signature header (fix.diff:1696-1716)
missing or empty signature -> reject instead of skip (fix.diff:1701-1702)
missing or empty secret -> reject fail-closed, replacing the allowEmpty path (fix.diff:1697-1698 and 1045-1079)
GitLab keeps verbatim token comparison (internal/openchoreo-api/services/git/gitlab.go:22-32, unchanged)
repository URL shapes: https with .git, git@host:path, ssh://, git+ssh://, trailing slash, uppercase (internal/openchoreo-api/services/autobuild/webhook_processor.go:343-362)
org/name path that contains another provider's domain, e.g. https://bitbucket.org/my-org/github.com-sync (fix.diff:1384-1388)
host that is not a known SaaS provider -> provider check skipped (fix.diff:1396-1397)

O7_producer.where: internal/openchoreo-api/services/autobuild/webhook_processor.go:180-241 (extractRepoInfoFromComponent: repository identity is mapped out of the Workflow/ClusterWorkflow openAPIV3Schema extensions plus the component parameters, with a schema-default fallback for branch)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A component whose repository URL does not parse to a host (schemeless like 'github.com/org/repo', or the slash form 'git@github.com/org/repo') still matches an attacker-forged webhook URL through matchesRepository's normalized string equality, but providerFromRepoURL returns "" for it, so the provider-consistency check is skipped and the build is triggered for a repository hosted on another provider.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Self-hosted GitLab/GitHub Enterprise and hand-written repository parameters are legitimate, and the provider cannot be inferred from an unknown host, so skipping the check is the documented, intended behaviour (fix.diff:1359-1362).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the repository match, one package away from the provider implementations; the two normalizers are in different packages (git and autobuild)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second caller of webhookProcessor.ProcessWebhook, e.g. a webhook redeliver/backfill CLI or admin endpoint
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The processor and its interface (service.go:26-28) are exported and take only provider+payload, so a maintainer adding a replay or migration tool would call it directly and bypass autobuildService.ProcessWebhook and therefore every signature check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a fourth provider (Gitea, Bitbucket Server/Data Center, Azure DevOps) added to GetProvider
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This switch is the project's documented extension point, and Bitbucket Server reuses X-Hub-Signature, so a maintainer would add it and could easily write ValidateWebhookPayload without wiring verifyHMACSHA256 - exactly the second-implementation shape this fix had to repair.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a portal 'test / simulate webhook' endpoint that calls AutoBuildService.ProcessWebhook with caller-supplied Signature and SignatureHeader
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ProcessWebhookParams lets any caller choose the signature header, signature and secret key, so a UI feature would pass empty values and reach the workflow-trigger sink without any signature.

O9_family: authentication bypass via webhook signature verification that fails open (CWE-287 improper authentication, CWE-290 authorization bypass by spoofing, CWE-345 insufficient verification of data authenticity)

O10_build.language: Go (go.mod:3 declares go 1.26.3; also Python agents and Helm charts in the same repo)
O10_build.toolchain: go build / go test; make go.test (make/golang.mk:170) runs manifests, generate, fmt, vet, envtest and then `go test $(go list ./... | grep -v /e2e)`; make openapi-codegen (make/golang.mk:186) regenerates internal/openchoreo-api/api/gen from openapi/openchoreo-api.yaml
O10_build.project_tests: internal/openchoreo-api/services/git (provider unit tests; bitbucket_test.go and signature.go are added by the fix), internal/openchoreo-api/services/autobuild (service_test.go and webhook_processor_test.go using the controller-runtime fake client via services/testutil/testutil.go:33), internal/openchoreo-api/api/handlers/webhook_handler_test.go; no cluster or network needed for these packages

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete the empty-token skip in BitbucketProvider.ValidateWebhookPayload (or make it reject anything that is not the secret) without plumbing X-Hub-Signature through detectGitProviderFromParams and the OpenAPI/generated params - the forgery is blocked, but every genuine Bitbucket webhook is now rejected because the handler still supplies an empty signature.

out_of_scope_notes: GitLab tokens are compared with plain != rather than constant time (internal/openchoreo-api/services/git/gitlab.go:27); that timing side channel is outside this advisory's protection and was not pursued.
The fix diff embeds a ~12k-line regenerated swaggerSpec blob in server.gen.go (fix.diff:71-952); it is mechanical and was not analysed line by line.
